name: jadx
why: A Dex-to-Java decompiler is a real window into Android apps, though it is well known in reversing circles.

brief.what_it_is: jadx is a command-line and GUI tool that turns Android app files into readable Java source code. It takes .apk, .dex, .aab, .xapk, .apkm, .apks and .zip files, plus Java .jar, .class and .aar files and .smali files. It writes out Java source and decoded resources, including AndroidManifest.xml decoded from resources.arsc. The jadx-gui front end adds syntax highlighting, jump to declaration, find usages and full-text search.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it simply as a "Dex to Java decompiler" and describes itself as "Command-line and GUI tools for producing Java source code from Android Dex and APK files". It does not state a broader motivation.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It says the tool decompiles Dalvik bytecode to Java, can also convert Java bytecode, and includes a deobfuscator. It also mentions a smali debugger in jadx-gui, with setup described on a wiki page.

Basic use: decompiles classes.dex and writes the output to the directory out.

Builds jadx from source; the README says JDK 17 or higher must be installed first. The output goes to build/jadx/bin and build/jadx-<version>.zip.

brief.install_notes: The README asks for 64-bit Java 11 or later, except for the with-jre bundle, which does not need it. On Windows, download the zip or the .exe bundle, and the Java installer link points to oracle.com. Arch, Homebrew and Flathub each have their own package. Building from source needs JDK 17 or higher and runs with ./gradlew dist (gradlew.bat on Windows). Optional environment variables set config, cache and temp directories (JADX_CONFIG_DIR, JADX_CACHE_DIR, JADX_TMP_DIR). Zip-bomb and XML security limits are on by default and can be turned off with environment variables. The README does not describe a first-run wizard.
brief.standout: It covers a wide input range in one tool: APKs, app bundles and split packages, plain Java classes, and smali. It also decodes binary resources, bundles a deobfuscator and a plugin marketplace command, and ships a GUI with a smali debugger. The README does not compare it with other decompilers, so any claim about its reputation rests on sources outside this page.
brief.status: The README has CI build-status, contributor, download and Maven Central badges, and it links to current Arch, Homebrew and Flathub packages. It also mentions a JDK 25 download link, which suggests recent upkeep. The README shows no release date or last-commit date, so I could not confirm the exact last release from the fetched text.
brief.caveats: The README warns that in most cases jadx "can't decompile 100% of the code, so errors will occur", and it points to a troubleshooting wiki page. It requires 64-bit Java 11 or later at runtime, and JDK 17 or higher to build from source. The licence is Apache 2.0. The README does not describe platform limits beyond the Windows bundles and the .bat files for double-click use.
